spots.name: Palacio Salvo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palacio Salvo is an eclectic skyscraper at the intersection of 18 de Julio Avenue and Plaza Independencia in the Centro neighbourhood of Montevideo, Uruguay.

spots.name: Plaza Independencia
spots.summary: Plaza Independencia is the main public square of Montevideo, Uruguay. It was laid out in the 19th century on the site formerly occupied by the Citadel of Montevideo, marking the transition between the old fortified city and the modern urban expansion.

spots.name: Legislative Palace
spots.summary: The Legislative Palace of Uruguay is a monumental building, meeting place of the General Assembly of Uruguay, and the seat of the legislative branch of the Uruguayan government. It is located in the Aguada neighborhood of Montevideo.

spots.name: Montevideo Metropolitan Cathedral
spots.summary: The Montevideo Metropolitan Cathedral is the main Roman Catholic church of Montevideo, and seat of its archdiocese. It is located right in front of the Cabildo across Constitution Square, in the neighbourhood of Ciudad Vieja.

spots.name: Rambla of Montevideo
spots.summary: The Rambla of Montevideo is the coastal avenue that goes along the coastline of the Rio de la Plata in Montevideo, Uruguay. At a length of over 22.2 uninterrupted kilometres (13.7 mi), the promenade runs along the Río de la Plata and continues down the entire coast of Montevideo.

spots.name: Solís Theatre
spots.summary: Solís Theatre is Uruguay's most important and renowned theater. It opened in 1856. The building was designed by the Italian architect Carlo Zucchi. It is located in Montevideo's Old Town, right next to the Plaza Independencia.

spots.name: 18 de Julio Avenue
spots.summary: Avenida 18 de Julio, or 18 de Julio Avenue, is the most important avenue in Montevideo, Uruguay. It is named after the date when the country's first Constitution was sworn in, on July 18, 1830.

spots.name: Artigas Mausoleum
spots.summary: The Artigas Mausoleum is a monument to Uruguayan hero José Artigas, located in Plaza Independencia, in the neighbourhood of Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo. It opened in 1977. Artigas's remains are kept in an underground room underneath the statue.

spots.name: Cerro Fortress
spots.summary: The Fortaleza del Cerro, also known as Fortaleza General Artigas, is a fortress situated in Montevideo, Uruguay overlooking the Bay of Montevideo. It belongs to the barrio of Casabó, at the west of Villa del Cerro.

spots.name: Estévez Palace
spots.summary: The Estévez Palace is a building located on Plaza Independencia in Montevideo, Uruguay. Completed in 1873, it served as the country’s seat of government from 1880 to 1985.

spots.name: Cerro de Montevideo
spots.summary: Cerro de Montevideo is a hill overlooking the namesake capital city of Uruguay. It constitutes an isolated landform, it is part of no mountain range.

spots.name: World Trade Center Montevideo
spots.summary: The World Trade Center Montevideo is a building complex located in Montevideo, Uruguay. It was officially opened in 1998, and renovated between 2002 and 2009.

spots.name: Constitution Square
spots.summary: Plaza de la Constitución, also known as Plaza Matriz, is the oldest city square in Montevideo, Uruguay.

spots.name: General Artigas railway station
spots.summary: General Artigas railway station is the former main railway station in Montevideo, Uruguay.

spots.name: Plaza de Cagancha
spots.summary: Plaza de Cagancha is a public square in the Centro neighborhood of Montevideo, Uruguay. Located on 18 de Julio Avenue, the main avenue of the city, it originated in 1836 as the central space of the layout of the "Ciudad Nueva", outside the limits of the walled area of the colonial period.

spots.name: Obelisk of Montevideo
spots.summary: The Obelisk of Montevideo, officially Obelisk to the Constituents of 1830 is a monument created by sculptor José Luis Zorrilla de San Martín (1891-1975). It is a three-sided obelisk made of granite, 40 metres (130 ft) tall with three bronze statues on its sides, representing "Law", "Liberty" and "Force".

spots.name: Mercado del Puerto
spots.summary: The Mercado del Puerto is a gastronomic and cultural venue in the Ciudad Vieja neighborhood of Montevideo, Uruguay. Originally built as a covered marketplace, it no longer functions as one and now houses restaurants serving traditional Uruguayan cuisine, with a focus on asado cooked over open-fire parrillas.

spots.name: Estadio Centenario
spots.summary: The Estadio Centenario is an association football stadium in Montevideo, Uruguay. Located in the Parque Batlle neighbourhood, it is owned by the Montevideo Department.

photo.author: Marcelo Campi from Costa de Oro, Uruguay

spots.name: Museo Torres García
spots.summary: The Museo Torres García is located in the historic Ciudad Vieja of Montevideo where unusual portraits of historical icons and cubist paintings akin to Picasso's paintings, painted by Joaquín Torres García are exhibited.

spots.name: Gateway of the Citadel
spots.summary: The Gateway of the Citadel is the only remaining piece of the military fortress that defended the walled city of Montevideo. The Citadel of Montevideo was a military fortress built by the Spanish in 1741 and demolished 1877.

spots.name: Palacio Municipal
spots.summary: The Palacio Municipal de Montevideo is the seat of Montevideo government, located on 18 de Julio Avenue, in Central Montevideo. It was designed by Uruguayan architect Mauricio Cravotto.

spots.name: National Museum of Natural History
spots.summary: The National Museum of Natural History in Montevideo is a natural history museum in Uruguay. It opened in 1838, and is the oldest scientific institution in Uruguay and one of the oldest natural history collections in the world.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of Natural History, Uruguay

spots.name: Palacio Taranco
spots.summary: Palacio Taranco, located in front of the Plaza Zabala, in the heart of the Old City of Montevideo, Uruguay, is a palace erected in the early 20th century during a period in which the architectural style was influenced by French architecture.

spots.name: Montevideo Cabildo
spots.summary: The Montevideo Cabildo is the public building in Montevideo that was used as the government house during the colonial times of the Viceroyalty of the River Plate. Today the building is used as a museum and houses the Historical Archive of the city. It is located on Constitution Square, in Ciudad Vieja.

photo.author: Área multimedia del Museo Hisórico Cabildo

spots.name: Plaza de la Diversidad Sexual
spots.summary: The Plaza de la Diversidad Sexual is located in the Old City neighborhood of Montevideo, Uruguay. The plaza includes a large triangular granite monolith -- a reference to the pink triangles worn during the Nazi persecution of LGBT people.

spots.name: National Museum of Visual Arts
spots.summary: National Museum of Visual Arts (Uruguay) (Spanish: Museo Nacional de Artes Visuales) a museum in Parque Rodó, Montevideo, Uruguay. It was inaugurated on December 10, 1911.

spots.name: Parque Prado
spots.summary: Parque Prado is the largest of Montevideo's six principal public parks. Established in 1873, it covers an area of 106 hectares and is located in the barrio of Prado. Located in the northern part of the city, the Miguelete Creek flows through the neighbourhood and park of the same name.

spots.name: Central Cemetery
spots.summary: The Central Cemetery of Barrio Sur, Montevideo, is one of the main cemeteries in Uruguay. It also ranks amongst the most popular in the country, given that most famous Uruguayan people are buried there.

spots.name: Punta Brava Lighthouse
spots.summary: Punta Brava Lighthouse, also known as Punta Carretas Lighthouse, is a lighthouse in Punta Carretas, Montevideo, Uruguay. It was erected in 1876. The lighthouse has a height of 21 metres and its light reaches 15 nautical miles away, with a flash every ten seconds. In 1962, the lighthouse became electric.

spots.name: Plaza Fabini
spots.summary: Plaza Fabini also known as Plaza del Entrevero, is a public square in the central business district of Montevideo, Uruguay. Located on 18 de Julio Avenue, on its north side starts Libertador Avenue.

spots.name: Avenida Italia
spots.summary: Italy Avenue is a major thoroughfare in Montevideo, Uruguay. Its name honors the country from whose immigrants about 40% of Uruguayans descend.

spots.name: Cathedral of The Most Holy Trinity, Montevideo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of The Most Holy Trinity, popularly known as "Templo Inglés", is an Anglican church in Montevideo, Uruguay.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of The Most Holy Trinity, Montevideo

spots.name: Biblioteca Nacional de Uruguay

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Biblioteca Nacional de Uruguay is the National Library of Uruguay, located in Montevideo. It was created in 1815 and is the legal deposit and copyright library for Uruguay. It has been located in its current building since 1955.

spots.name: Artigas Boulevard
spots.summary: Artigas Boulevard is a boulevard in Montevideo, Uruguay. It runs from the Rambla at Punta Carretas to the Rambla at Capurro-Bella Vista, going north for about 6.5 kilometers and turning 100° west.

spots.name: Plaza Zabala
spots.summary: Plaza Zabala is a plaza in the Ciudad Vieja of Montevideo, Uruguay. In late 1878, during the dictatorship of Colonel Lorenzo Latorre, it was decided to demolish the old fort and build a public square in its place. But for 12 years this site remained a wasteland.

spots.name: Cementerio del Buceo
spots.summary: Cementerio del Buceo is a cemetery in Montevideo, Uruguay. It was established in 1872.

spots.name: The British Cemetery Montevideo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The British Cemetery of Montevideo is one of the oldest operating cemeteries in Uruguay.

spots.name: Santos Palace
spots.summary: The Santos Palace is a neoclassical building located in the Centro neighborhood of Montevideo, Uruguay. Built in the 1880s, it serves as the protocol headquarters of the country's Ministry of Foreign Relations.

spots.name: Japanese Garden
spots.summary: The Japanese Garden of Montevideo is located in the Prado neighbourhood of Montevideo, behind the Juan Manuel Blanes Museum.

spots.name: Club Uruguay
spots.summary: Club Uruguay is a gentlemen's club located in Montevideo, Uruguay.

spots.name: Santuario Nacional del Corazón de Jesús

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Shrine of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, popularly known as Iglesia del Cerrito is a Roman Catholic parish church and national shrine in Montevideo, Uruguay.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Santuario Nacional del Corazón de Jesús, Montevideo

spots.name: Alfredo Vásquez Acevedo Institute
spots.summary: The Instituto Alfredo Vásquez Acevedo is a public high school in Montevideo, Uruguay. Identified as Liceo No. 35 of Montevideo, it was named in honor of the jurist and politician Alfredo Vásquez Acevedo.

spots.name: Parroquia San Francisco de Asís

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Parish Church of St. Francis of Assisi is a Roman Catholic parish church in Montevideo, Uruguay.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Parroquia San Francisco de Asís, Montevideo

spots.name: Palacio Rinaldi
spots.summary: Palacio Rinaldi is a building in Centro, Montevideo, Uruguay, located on the Plaza Independencia near its junction with the 18 de Julio Avenue, near the Palacio Salvo.

spots.name: Libertador Avenue
spots.summary: Libertador Avenue is a major avenue in Montevideo, Uruguay.

spots.name: Edificio Lapido
spots.summary: Lapido Building, also known as Lapido Palace, is a modernist building in Montevideo, Uruguay, located on 18 de Julio Avenue in the city centre.

spots.name: Ateneo de Montevideo
spots.summary: The Athenæum of Montevideo is a cultural institution in Montevideo, Uruguay. Founded on July 3, 1886 with the merger of the Sociedad Universitaria and the Ateneo del Uruguay, it is housed in an eclectic-historicist style building located on the Plaza de Cagancha in Centro.

spots.name: Estadio Gran Parque Central
spots.summary: The Estadio Gran Parque Central is the stadium of Club Nacional de Football located in Montevideo, Uruguay, near Nacional headquarters, in the La Blanqueada neighbourhood.

spots.name: Casa Matriz del Banco República
spots.summary: The Headquarters of the Bank of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay is the building that houses the main offices of the Banco de la República Oriental del Uruguay. It is located in Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Headquarters of the Bank of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay

spots.name: Mercado Modelo
spots.summary: Mercado Modelo was the central municipal fruit and vegetable wholesale market in of Montevideo, Uruguay. The area around the installations, which occupy several blocks of the Mercado Modelo–Bolívar barrio, has also taken on the name of the market, hence the composite name of the entire barrio.

spots.name: Holocaust Memorial, Montevideo
spots.summary: The Memorial to the Holocaust of the Jewish People is an outdoor memorial dedicated to victims of the Holocaust.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of Our Lady of Bzommar is the cathedral church of the Armenian Catholic Church in Prado (Montevideo), Uruguay as Co-cathedral of Armenian Catholic Apostolic Exarchate of Latin America and Mexico.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of Our Lady of Bzommar

spots.name: Saint Nicholas Greek

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Saint Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church is an Eastern Orthodox church building located in the grounds of the headquarters of the Greek Community in Prado neighbourhood in Montevideo, Uruguay.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Saint Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church, Montevideo

spots.name: Teatro de Verano
spots.summary: The Teatro de Verano, officially known as Teatro de Verano Ramón Collazo is an open-air amphitheatre in the Parque Rodó neighbourhood of Montevideo, Uruguay. It was inaugurated in January 1944 and has a seating capacity of approximately 5,000.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora del Sagrado Corazón, Montevideo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Our Lady of the Sacred Heart, popularly known as Iglesia Punta Carretas is a Roman Catholic parish church in Montevideo, Uruguay.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Nuestra Señora del Sagrado Corazón, Montevideo

spots.name: Museum of Pre-Columbian and Indigenous Art
spots.summary: The Museum of Pre-Columbian and Indigenous Art is an ethnographic museum located in Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo, Uruguay, dedicated to the indigenous cultures of different parts of Latin America.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Pre-Columbian and Indigenous Art

spots.name: Carnival Museum
spots.summary: The Carnival Museum is located at 25 De Mayo Street in the "Ciudad Vieja" in Montevideo, Uruguay. It was built in November 2006.

spots.name: UTE Museum
spots.summary: The Museo de UTE is a museum located in Barrio Centro in Montevideo, Uruguay. Specialized in the history, science and technology of Uruguay, the museum is directly dependent on the UTE. It exposes diverse elements linked to the history of the Uruguayan company.

spots.name: Museo Gurvich
spots.summary: Museo Gurvich is an art museum in Montevideo, Uruguay, dedicated to preserving the art of José Gurvich, an important Constructivist painter, founded in 2001. It opened to the public in 2005.

spots.name: Cinemateca Uruguaya

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cinemateca Uruguaya is a non-profit cinematheque in Montevideo, Uruguay, established in 1952, that aims to support the cultural development of cinema, and of art in general. Since its inception, it has belonged to the International Federation of Film Archives (FIAF).

spots.name: Torre Ejecutiva

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The current presidential office, next to the former. The Executive Tower was first planned as a courthouse in the 1960s, the project was halted several times until the house was finalized as the presidential office in 2009.

spots.name: Torre de las Telecomunicaciones

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 157 m high, this skyscraper is Uruguay's highest building. There's a viewing platform and even free guided tours (in Spanish).

spots.name: Hipodromo Nacional de Maroñas
spots.summary: Accessible by car or taxi because surrounding neighborhoods are not the safest it is a great place to spend a weekend afternoon at the horse races. The building is absolutely gorgeous build in 1874 surrounded by a beautiful park a horse pool and the track. They have a restaurant and you can see the races and have drinks on the terrace. There is plenty to see for children and space for running arou

spots.name: Museo del Fútbol
spots.summary: It's in the stadium where the first football world championships were held in 1930. You can see old photos, flags, jerseys, posters, trophies, flags and such. You will also get access to the stadium itself (unless there is a game going on).

spots.name: Castillo Pittamiglio
spots.summary: Eccentric small brick castle at the beach. A guided tour, arranged four times a week, is the only way to see the inside of the castle.

spots.name: Fuente de los Candados
spots.summary: A small fountain at corner of Yi, completely covered by locks. Similar to bridges in many European cities, couples come here to attach a padlock to it. If they do so their love is supposed to last forever and they will also return to Montevideo someday.
